Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to administer the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns related to your postpartum experience. The EPDS screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource in helping us provide the best possible care for you during this time.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and is intended to create a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself honestly. I'm here to listen and provide guidance, not to judge. Our goal is to work together to ensure you receive the care and support you need as a new mother.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your feelings and experiences over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you'd like. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this process as comfortable and supportive as possible.

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself and your ability to cope with your new role as a mother?

.. to be honest, it's been a bit of a struggle. I mean, I'm trying my best, but some days I just feel so tired and overwhelmed. Taking care of the baby is a lot of work, and I feel like I'm always worrying about whether I'm doing everything right. Like, is the baby eating enough? Is the baby healthy? Those kinds of thoughts just keep running through my head, and it's hard to shut them off. 

Sometimes I feel like I'm managing okay, but other times I just feel like I'm barely keeping my head above water. I get anxious about little things, like if the baby is crying and I don't know how to calm them down. It's like, I know I should be able to handle it, but in that moment, it just feels so overwhelming. 

I don't feel like I'm failing or anything, but I do feel like I could use some extra support sometimes. It's just hard to balance everything and take care of myself too. I feel like I'm putting all my energy into taking care of the baby, and then I'm just exhausted. So, I guess you could say I'm coping, but it's not always easy.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah... I'd say that's still there for me, but not as much as it used to be. I mean, I can still laugh and find the humor in things, but it's just not as frequent as it was before the baby was born. Some days, I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and it's hard to find the energy to laugh or enjoy things like I used to. 

But, you know, when my baby smiles at me or does something cute, it still melts my heart and makes me laugh. Those moments are really special, and they help me feel more connected to my baby and to myself. It's just... those moments are kind of fleeting, and then I'm back to feeling overwhelmed and worried about everything again. 

I don't feel like I've lost my sense of humor completely, though. I just feel like it's been muted a bit, you know? Like, I can still appreciate the funny side of things, but it's just not as strong as it was before. Does that make sense?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

To be honest, I haven't really been looking forward to things as much as I used to. I mean, before the baby was born, I would get excited about little things like going out with friends or trying a new restaurant. But now, it's just hard to muster up the energy to think about those things, let alone look forward to them.

I feel like my whole world has kind of shrunk down to just taking care of the baby and getting through each day. I don't really have the mental space to think about fun things I want to do or look forward to. And when I do try to think about it, I just feel guilty because I'm like, "I should be focusing on the baby, not thinking about myself."

It's not that I don't enjoy spending time with my baby - I do! But it's just that everything feels so overwhelming and exhausting right now. I don't really have the capacity to think about things I enjoy or look forward to them like I used to. Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah... I'd say that's definitely been happening to me lately. As a new mom, I feel like I'm already questioning everything I do, and when things don't go exactly as planned, I tend to beat myself up over it. Like, if the baby is crying and I don't know how to calm them down, I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I soothe my own baby?" Or, if I'm not producing enough milk, I'll think, "I'm a failure as a mom, I'm not even providing for my baby's basic needs."

It's like, I know intellectually that these things aren't my fault, and that every mom goes through struggles like this. But in the moment, it's hard not to take it personally and blame myself. I feel like I'm already walking on eggshells, trying to do everything just right, and when things don't go as planned, it's easy to fall into that pattern of self-blame.

It's not all the time, but it's definitely been happening more often since the baby was born. And it's not just about the baby, either - I'll also blame myself for little things, like not being able to keep the house clean or not being able to cook a decent meal. It's like, I'm already feeling so overwhelmed and exhausted, and then I'll just pile on the self-blame, and it makes everything feel even worse.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's definitely been happening to me a lot lately. I'd say it's mostly related to the baby's health and well-being, but sometimes it just feels like I'm worrying for no good reason at all. Like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll just start thinking about all these worst-case scenarios. "What if the baby stops breathing?" "What if I'm not producing enough milk?" "What if the baby gets sick?" It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these terrible thoughts, and I don't know how to stop it.

And it's not just about the baby, either. Sometimes I'll worry about things that are totally unrelated to the baby, like "What if something happens to my partner?" or "What if we can't pay our bills?" It's like, my brain just gets stuck in this cycle of worry and anxiety, and I don't know how to get out of it.

It's hard to explain, but it feels like my brain is just constantly "on" now, like I'm always on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. And even when everything is fine, and the baby is healthy and happy, I still can't shake this feeling of anxiety. It's like, I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know?

Sometimes I try to talk to my partner about it, but even they don't always understand what I'm going through. They'll be like, "Oh, don't worry, everything will be fine," but it's hard to just "not worry" when you're in the midst of all these anxious thoughts. Does that make sense?
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times since the baby was born. It's like, I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's really scary, because I don't know what's causing it, and I don't know how to make it stop.

Sometimes it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the baby gets hurt, or what if I'm not doing something right? And then I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sense of fear and panic. It's like, my brain is just spiraling out of control, and I don't know how to calm it down.

It's not all the time, but it's happened enough that it's really started to worry me. I'll be okay, and then suddenly I'll just feel this panic rising up, and I'll be like, "What's wrong with me? Why am I feeling like this?" It's really hard to explain, but it's like my body is just reacting to some kind of invisible threat, and I don't know how to make it stop.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to put into words. I'll just be like, "I feel scared, and I don't know why," and they'll be like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know, that's the thing. Nothing's wrong, but I just feel this way." It's really frustrating, because I feel like I should be able to control my own emotions, but sometimes I just can't.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's definitely been true for me lately. It feels like everything is just piling up, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I mean, I love my baby, and I'm so grateful to be a mom, but it's just so overwhelming. The sleep deprivation, the constant worrying, the pressure to do everything just right... it all just feels like it's getting on top of me.

Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll just start to feel like I'm drowning in all of the responsibilities. The laundry, the dishes, the cooking, the cleaning... it's all just so much. And on top of that, I'm trying to take care of this tiny human who is completely dependent on me. It's a lot of pressure, and sometimes I just feel like I'm not doing enough.

I'll have days where I feel like I'm managing okay, but then something will happen, like the baby will have a fussy day, or I'll get a phone call from a family member who's stressing me out, and it just feels like everything is getting on top of me. I'll feel like I'm at my breaking point, and I don't know how to keep going.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, and sometimes I feel like I'm going to sink. But at the same time, I don't want to admit that I'm struggling, because I feel like I should be able to handle it all. I feel like I should be a better mom, a better partner, a better person. So, I just try to push through, and hope that things will get easier eventually.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been true for me lately. I've been having a lot of trouble sleeping, and I think it's because I've been feeling really unhappy and overwhelmed. Even when I'm exhausted, I'll lie in bed and my mind will just start racing with all of the things that are worrying me. I'll think about the baby, and whether I'm doing everything right, and whether I'm a good mom. I'll think about all of the things I need to do, and how I'm going to get everything done. And I'll just feel this sense of sadness and anxiety that I don't know how to shake.

Sometimes I'll fall asleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of unhappiness. It's like, my brain is just stuck in this cycle of worry and anxiety, and I don't know how to turn it off. I'll try to calm myself down, and tell myself that everything will be okay, but it's hard to shake the feeling of sadness and unrest.

It's not that I'm unhappy all the time, but it's just that the stress and anxiety of being a new mom is really getting to me. And when I'm lying in bed at night, it's like all of those feelings just come flooding back, and I don't know how to deal with them. I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but even they don't always understand what I'm going through. They'll be like, "Just try to relax, and get some sleep," but it's not that easy. It's like, my brain is just wired to worry and stress, and I don't know how to turn it off.

I've had a few nights where I've just cried myself to sleep, because I feel so overwhelmed and unhappy. It's like, I'm just trying to keep it all together, but sometimes it feels like everything is just falling apart. And when I'm lying in bed at night, it's like all of those feelings just come crashing down on me, and I don't know how to cope.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's definitely been true for me lately. I'd say it's been a pretty regular feeling since the baby was born. Some days are better than others, but overall, I just feel this underlying sense of sadness and melancholy. It's like, I'm happy to be a mom and I love my baby, but at the same time, I just feel so overwhelmed and unhappy.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, without really feeling like myself. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like, I'm just trying to get through each day, without really feeling like I'm living.

Sometimes I'll have a good day, and I'll think to myself, "Okay, I'm doing okay. I'm managing." But then the next day will come, and I'll just feel like I'm back at square one. It's like, I'm just trying to find my footing as a new mom, but it's hard when I'm feeling so sad and overwhelmed all the time.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to put into words. I'll just be like, "I'm feeling really sad and overwhelmed," and they'll be like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know. I just feel like I'm not doing enough, and I'm not being a good mom." And they'll try to reassure me, but it's hard to shake the feeling of sadness and inadequacy.

It's not all the time, but it's definitely been a regular feeling for me since the baby was born. And it's hard, because I feel like I should be happy and grateful to be a new mom, but instead, I just feel sad and overwhelmed.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's happened to me a few times since the baby was born. I'd say it's not a daily thing, but it's definitely happened more often than I'd like to admit. I'll just be sitting there, feeding the baby or trying to get them to sleep, and suddenly I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and frustration. And before I know it, I'm crying.

It's like, I'm just trying to hold it all together, but sometimes it's just too much. The lack of sleep, the pressure to be a perfect mom, the stress of taking care of a new baby... it all just gets to me, and I'll just break down in tears. Sometimes it's just a few tears, but other times it's a full-on sobbing fit.

It's hard, because I feel like I should be able to handle it all, but sometimes I just can't. And when I start crying, it's like I'm just releasing all of the emotions that I've been trying to hold inside. It's like, I'm just so overwhelmed and unhappy, and I don't know how to make it stop.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, and they're always really supportive and try to reassure me that everything will be okay. But it's hard, because even with their support, I still feel like I'm just not doing enough, and that I'm not being a good mom. And that feeling of inadequacy just makes me feel even more unhappy and tearful.

It's not something that I'm proud of, but it's just something that's been happening to me lately. And I guess it's just a sign that I need to take care of myself a bit better, and maybe reach out for some extra support. Because being a new mom is hard, and it's okay to not be okay sometimes.
